title: Physics on arXiv — latest announcement batch, 9 October 2026
global_caveat: arXiv publishes no official trending chart. This is an inferred notable-paper selection, not a popularity ranking; citation momentum and independent attention evidence were sparse for papers only hours old.

sections.title: Observation of single top-quark production in the s-channel in proton-proton collisions at sqrt(s)=13 TeV with the ATLAS detector
sections.abstract: ATLAS reports the first single-experiment observation of s-channel single-top production, using 140 fb^-1 of 13 TeV proton-proton data and a graph-neural-network analysis.
sections.claimed_result: The fitted cross-section is 10.8 ± 1.5 (stat.) ± 1.6 (syst.) pb, consistent with the Standard Model prediction, according to the ATLAS analysis.
sections.evidence_type: Experimental; 140 fb^-1 of 13 TeV ATLAS collision data, analyzed with a graph neural network and likelihood fit.
sections.unique_caveat: The result is one experiment's analysis; the quoted cross-section retains sizable statistical and systematic uncertainties.

sections.title: Evidence for Normal Neutrino Ordering with Combined Atmospheric Neutrino Experiments
sections.abstract: A joint fit to public atmospheric-neutrino data from Super-Kamiokande, IceCube-DeepCore, and KM3NeT/ORCA favors normal over inverted neutrino mass ordering.
sections.claimed_result: The analysis prefers normal ordering with Δχ²=11.0 and excludes inverted ordering at 99.95% confidence (3.3σ) after pseudoexperiment calibration.
sections.evidence_type: Experimental; simultaneous fit to publicly available atmospheric-neutrino samples from three detector programs.
sections.unique_caveat: The preference is below discovery-level significance and remains conditional on the data selections, detector-response models, and treatment of shared systematics.

sections.title: JWST CAPERS: Spectroscopic evaluation of very high redshift galaxy candidates
sections.abstract: Spectroscopy of 183 JWST-selected candidates tests high-redshift selection methods, confirming 48 galaxies at z≥8.5 and finding the sample's highest spectroscopic redshift at z=12.98.
sections.claimed_result: In this sample, using a UV-luminosity-function prior raises the high-redshift confirmation success rate from about 35% to 77%, with greater completeness than conservative cuts.
sections.evidence_type: Observational; JWST/NIRSpec PRISM spectroscopy and NIRCam-selected CAPERS candidates.
sections.unique_caveat: The reported efficiency applies to this survey sample and its selection; the authors find no confirmed source above z=13.

sections.title: Discovery of Hidden Extragalactic Pulsars in the Parkes Archival Data
sections.abstract: Reprocessing the Parkes Magellanic-Cloud pulsar surveys with more sensitive candidate-folding methods finds six pulsars, five in the Large Magellanic Cloud.
sections.claimed_result: The discoveries raise the known Large Magellanic Cloud radio-pulsar count to 49; the authors' population analysis finds consistency with Galactic canonical pulsars.
sections.evidence_type: Observational; reanalysis of original Parkes Multibeam Magellanic-Cloud survey data.
sections.unique_caveat: The SMC-direction detection is identified as a Milky Way foreground pulsar; population-synthesis projections depend on adopted upper limits.

sections.title: A quasiparticle-protected superconducting qubit
sections.abstract: A niobium-ground-plane transmon with strongly gap-engineered aluminium junctions tolerates over an order of magnitude more near-infrared optical power before excess relaxation appears than a comparable all-aluminium device.
sections.claimed_result: The niobium device shows no resolvable quasiparticle-induced frequency shift over the tested power range, while relaxation remains protected relative to the control transmon.
sections.evidence_type: Experimental; optical-power tests of flux-tunable superconducting transmons.
sections.unique_caveat: Dephasing and state-preparation-and-measurement infidelity still worsen as optical power rises; the work does not remove all light-induced errors.

sections.title: First demonstration of 50ps four-dimensional vertex reconstruction with the Timepix4 beam telescope
sections.abstract: Beam-test data demonstrate four-dimensional track-and-vertex reconstruction with tens-of-picoseconds timing using a silicon-pixel telescope.
sections.claimed_result: With 16 timing-plane clusters, the measured vertex-time resolution is 54 ± 5 ps; the fitted model includes an irreducible component of 29.2 ± 0.6 ps.
sections.evidence_type: Experimental; 180 GeV/c mixed-hadron beam on a fixed target at the CERN SPS and Timepix4 telescope measurements.
sections.unique_caveat: The residual floor includes clock-distribution and time-reference contributions, so it is not solely a limit of the sensor or reconstruction method.

sections.title: Listening to the Horizon: Probing Near-Horizon Reflectivity with GW250114
sections.abstract: A search for delayed gravitational-wave echoes in GW250114 finds no evidence for them and constrains the reflectivity of a putative compact-object surface.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report no echo evidence and derive a 90% credible upper bound |R_s|<0.06, corresponding to reflected energy below 0.4%, under their echo model.
sections.evidence_type: Observational; quasinormal-mode-filtered analysis of GW250114 using an echo template normalized to the reported prompt Direct Wave.
sections.unique_caveat: The interpretation depends on the template and on whether the prompt Direct Wave carries near-horizon information; the authors explicitly note that this is unsettled.

sections.title: Cavity Characterization for the Princeton Axion Search
sections.abstract: Measurements and simulations of the Princeton Axion Search cavity validate its mode structure and quantify form-factor uncertainty for a planned sub-μeV axion search.
sections.claimed_result: Bead-perturbation measurements agree with simulations for the cavity modes and TM010 field profile; welded seams and end-cap joints do not significantly degrade Q.
sections.evidence_type: Experimental and computational; cavity measurements combined with electromagnetic simulations for the Princeton Axion Search.
sections.unique_caveat: This is a cavity-characterization paper, not an axion detection; the planned search's eventual sensitivity also depends on operating and noise performance.
